questions.question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The efforts of the Government in providing health education and Primary Health Centres __**is borne**__ fruits.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'** i.e.** "have borne".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **subject **of the sentence, **"efforts**," is** plural.**
 
• Thus, the **verb** form** should also be plural**, hence **"have" instead** of "is" or "has".
 
• The past participle form **"borne"** is correctly used, which is the past participle of **"bear"** in the sense of producing or yielding something.

Therefore, the **sentence should **be: *"The efforts of the Government in providing health education and Primary Health Centres **have borne** fruits."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Now, let's look at the meanings of the other options:
 
 
• **"has borne" **would be correct if the subject of the sentence was singular.
 
• **"was bore" **is grammatically incorrect. The correct past participle of "bear" is "borne" when it means to produce or yield something, and "was" should not be used with "borne" in this context.

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option "No error".**

We talked about writing a will, but it/ was one of those thing you never/ get around to doing.

options.text: was one of those thing you never
We talked about writing a will, but it

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **segment** of the sentence **that contains a grammatical error** is *"was one of those thing you never".*
 
• In the phrase** "one of those things"**, the word **"things"** should be** plural **because "one of" is referring to any one member of a group or category.
 
• The **group or category** (in this case, "things") is always **plural** in this construction.

Therefore, the correct sentence should be:* "We talked about writing a will, but it** was one of those things you never** get around to doing."*

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the correct passive form of the sentence.

Daniel and Mary invited us to their wedding.

options.text: We have been invited to Daniel and Mary’s wedding.
We were invited to Daniel and Mary’s wedding.
We are invited to Daniel and Mary’s wedding.
We had been invited to Daniel and Mary’s wedding.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In English, the **passive voice is formed by **using the verb 'to be' + past participle (V3) of the main verb.
 
• The **past participle** of 'invite' is **'invited'.**
 
• The **original sentence** is in the** simple past** tense, and hence the passive form should also be in the simple past tense.
 
• Therefore,** 'were invited' **is the** correct** form.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is:* 'We were invited to Daniel and Mary’s wedding.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Now, let's look at the other options:
 
 
• **"We have been invited to Daniel and Mary’s wedding."** This sentence is in the present perfect tense, not the simple past tense.
 
• **"We are invited to Daniel and Mary’s wedding."** This sentence is in the present simple tense, not the simple past tense.
 
• **"We had been invited to Daniel and Mary’s wedding**." This sentence is in the past perfect tense, not the simple past tense.

questions.question:

Q. hold in their hands and get their head

R. to work with, a physical object they can

S. round and low-cost 3D printers make that possible
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **P: **This part **introduces the idea** that people learn better when they can interact with something tangible.
 
• **R: **This part **completes the thought** started in P and gives specifics - a physical object that they can work with.
 
• **Q: **It **further elaborates on the idea** of tangibility, stating that they can hold it in their hands and wrap their head around it.
 
• **S: **This **part introduces the solution** - low-cost 3D printers - which make the previously described scenario possible.

Therefore, the **correct sequence** is: **'PRQS'**. i.e. *"Many people learn better when they have something tangible to work with, a physical object they can hold in their hands and get their head round and low-cost 3D printers make that possible."*

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

“I have heard the podcast before,” Nita says.

options.text: Nita says that she is hearing the podcast before.
Nita says that she had heard the podcast before.
Nita says that she has heard the podcast before.
Nita says that she had heard the podcast ago.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Here, Nita's **experience of having heard** the podcast before is still a relevant fact when she is reporting it, so the **present perfect tense** ("has heard") will be retained in the reported speech.
 
• When the Direct Speech is in **Present Tense** (in this case, 'says') or **Future Tense,** there is** no change** in the Indirect Speech.
 
• **'Has'** will be used instead of **'Have'** as we use '**Has'** with singular noun or singular pronoun.
